title: Tsuruoka — 鶴岡
goal: Connect a difficult bird name with common bird/body words and listening.

cards.title: Observe Rather than Memorise a Difficult Name

blocks.text: Tsuruoka has a rich food culture and includes Kamo Aquarium. We will borrow an imaginary nature photograph and an audio scene, without implying that cranes are guaranteed at any attraction.
**鶴岡で写真を見ます。** つるおかで しゃしんを みます。 — I look at photographs in Tsuruoka.

Today we formally study a common bird character and a few body words. The difficult crane character stays assisted. The learner should be able to understand a city name without being tested on every rare reading of its spelling.

items: **Character:** 鶴 · **Meaning/reading:** crane; つる, カク · **Radical/components:** 鳥, とり, on the right; 隺 on the left, containing a cover-like top over a 隹-like bird form · **Role:** Encounter. 隺 contributes to historical sound/meaning structure; it is not a new required word.
**Character:** 岡 · **Meaning/reading:** hill; おか, コウ · **Radical/components:** 山, やま, within a framed modern structure · **Role:** Encounter review from 盛岡.

blocks.text: **鶴岡 / つるおか**. The bird radical gives a relevant clue, while the word and city reading remain learned forms. Compare **盛岡 / もりおか**: both share 岡. The same tail of a name helps recognition, not geographic identification of the entire place.

**鳥 / とり — bird.** 鳥 is its own radical, とり. Its complete bird-derived shape has a head/body area and four lower dot strokes. Recognise it as a whole. The dots are not automatically an independent 火 word just because some other radicals have a similar bottom form.
**鳥がいます。** とりが います。 — There is a bird.
**あの鳥は白いです。** あの とりは しろいです。 — That bird over there is white.
A live bird uses います. The animal word 鳥 differs from **鶏肉 / とりにく**, chicken meat, which will be assisted food vocabulary later. Do not assume every bird mentioned is a food item.

**目 / め — eye; 目が二つ / めがふたつ — two eyes, in a simple count phrase.** 目 is its own radical, め. Its enclosed structure has more internal horizontal division than 日. Whole-shape recognition prevents confusing an eye with a day.
**目で見ます。** めで みます。 — I see with my eyes.

で can mark the means/instrument, extending the transport example **電車で行きます**. This statement is a simple body-word model, not a medical lesson. The phrase count uses the general item counter already learned in Hachinohe; we do not introduce a specialist body-part counter.
**耳 / みみ — ear.** 耳 is its own radical, みみ. The whole ear-derived shape has side strokes extending beyond the interior horizontal lines. Notice how its outline differs from 目.
**これは耳です。** これは みみです。 — This is an ear, in an illustrated label exercise.
**耳で聞きます。** みみで ききます。 — I listen with my ears.

聞く is introduced with its reading now and explained next. Body labels should point clearly to a drawing. We avoid vague guessing between 目 and 耳 when no image or meaning cue is supplied. Both words can be recognised independently even before wider body vocabulary is studied.
**足 / あし — foot; leg.** 足 is its own radical, あし. Notice a top 口-like section above a lower foot/step-related shape. These recognition pieces do not mean “mouth below.”
**鳥の足 / とりのあし — a bird's feet/legs.**
**あの鳥には足が二つあります。** あの とりには あしが ふたつ あります。 — That bird has two legs, in our illustration.

The body parts use あります in this sentence; the living bird itself uses います. Grammar can express possession/parts. An animal's being alive does not force every noun associated with it to take います. This example makes that distinction explicit.

**聞く / きく — hear; listen; ask.** Radical **耳**, みみ, inside **門**, もんがまえ, a gate-shaped enclosure. Hearing is a useful meaning connection; the visible gate is not a promise that listening only occurs at a gate.
**音を聞きます。** おとを ききます。 — I listen to a sound.
**音 / おと — sound**, assisted 音. **声 / こえ — voice**, assisted 声. **鳥の声を聞きます。** とりの こえを ききます。 — I listen to a bird's voice/call.
The noun before を tells us what is heard. The verb keeps 聞 in 聞きます/聞きました. Do not confuse it with 見る, seeing.
**友だちに聞きます。** ともだちに ききます。 — I ask a friend.
**友だちに駅の場所を聞きます。** ともだちに えきの ばしょを ききます。 — I ask a friend about the station's location.

場所 / ばしょ is reviewed as an assisted word from earlier place lessons. に identifies the person asked in this pattern; を identifies the requested information. In **鳥の声を聞きます**, 聞く means listen; in our person/information scene it means ask. Learn the whole sentence relationship rather than give every occurrence one rigid English translation.
**文を読みます。** ぶんを よみます。 — I read a sentence.
**友だちの声を聞きます。** ともだちの こえを ききます。 — I listen to my friend's voice.
**写真を見ます。** しゃしんを みます。 — I look at a photograph.

Reading, listening and seeing are different actions that can all use を for their object. The choice of verb depends on the activity. **音楽 / おんがく — music**, an assisted whole word; 音/楽 stay encounters. **音楽を聞きました。** おんがくを ききました。 — I listened to music. The new action reuses a familiar past ending.
**鶴岡で白い鳥を見ました。鳥の声を聞きました。** つるおかで しろい とりを みました。とりの こえを ききました。 — I saw a white bird in Tsuruoka. I listened to its call.
**その鳥には足が二つあります。** その とりには あしが ふたつ あります。 — That bird has two legs.

This is a fictional observation. It does not identify the species as a crane just because the city name includes 鶴. The words and grammar provide evidence; a name gloss cannot supply an unstated detail about the actual bird.

items: Read 鶴岡, 鳥, 目, 耳 and 足. **Answer:** つるおか; とり; め; みみ; あし.
Which radical is inside 聞? **Answer:** 耳.
Choose the live-bird verb: 鳥がいます / 鳥があります. **Answer:** 鳥がいます, for the stated live bird.
Which noun means an eye? **Answer:** 目.
Complete “ask a friend”: 友だち＿聞きます。 **Answer:** に.
Is the white bird automatically a crane because the city is Tsuruoka? **Answer:** No; the observation has not identified its species.

blocks.text: 鶴岡 is つるおか. 鶴 remains assisted, while 鳥 becomes formal study. 目/耳/足 are め/みみ/あし. A live animal uses います; a stated body part can use あります. 聞く can mean hear/listen or ask; the object and person pattern clarify it. Read is 読む; see is 見る.
**Recall task:** “I ask a friend about the station's location.” **Model:** 友だちに駅の場所を聞きます。 Continue to Sakata and describe a home rather than only a temporary visit.
